6.subject: MesgBroadcaster::RemoveListener(HrvValue): erase by hand-written compaction
6.body:
What: replaces std::find + vector::erase with a manual pointer scan and a shift-down, then pop_back.
Why it might be faster: it avoids the generic algorithm and erase machinery. Honest note: this function is a listener-registry call, not on the per-record decode path, so the 0.1% search-time step is most likely noise that the ordering heuristic accepted. Keep it only as part of the series, not as evidence of a real gain.

11.subject: Decode::Resume: keep byte index/offset in locals inside the read loop
11.body:
What: copies currentByteIndex/currentByteOffset into local variables for the per-byte loop and writes them back only when control leaves the loop (message, pause, end of file). Also re-indents tab-indented lines.
Why it might be faster: members are reloaded and stored on every byte because ReadByte may alias them; locals can stay in registers. The step measured 0.4% at search time, i.e. close to the instrument's noise floor.
Risk: the pause/resume bookkeeping is rewritten; the harness checksum matched, but only the benchmark files were exercised.

12.subject: Profile::GetFieldIndex: cache a field-number -> index table for the last message
12.body:
What: keeps a function-local static table (256 entries + presence bitmap) for the most recently queried message and answers repeated queries in O(1) instead of scanning mesg->fields.
Why it might be faster: the decoder asks for the same message's field indices over and over; the linear scan becomes a bit test and an array read.
Risk: the cache is unsynchronised static state, so concurrent callers from several threads would race. The benchmark is single-threaded and the checksum matched; thread safety was not tested.

13.subject: FieldBase::FieldBase(const FieldBase&): initialise members in the init-list
13.body:
What: copies values and stringIndexes in the member-initialiser list instead of default-constructing both vectors and assigning them in the body.
Why it might be faster: saves two default constructions and two assignments per copy; fields are copied constantly while building messages. This is the largest single step of the series that has a clear mechanism (about 4% at search time).

17.subject: Profile::GetMesg(num): replace the linear scan with a lazily built lookup table
17.body:
What: the first call builds a 65536-entry static table num -> index; later calls are one array read.
Why it might be faster: GetMesg was a linear scan over all message types, called for every message record. Biggest step in this series (about 6% at search time).
Risk: lazy initialisation uses a plain bool flag, so the first calls from several threads would race. Not tested. Costs 128 KB of static memory.

18.subject: Field::GetType: single-return form
18.body:
What: restructures the early returns into one condition. Behaviour is unchanged.
Why it might be faster: probably it is not; the step measured 0.03% and is noise. Included only because the search accepted it.

20.subject: CRC::Get16: byte-wise table built at compile time
20.body:
What: replaces the two-nibble, 16-entry table with a 256-entry constexpr table (same CRC-16, polynomial 0xA001) and processes one byte per lookup.
Why it might be faster: half the table lookups and no nibble shuffling per byte; CRC runs over every file byte. Step measured 0.25% (small). Checksum identical.

21.subject: Mesg::AddField(const Field&): scan fields directly instead of calling GetField
21.body:
What: loops over the existing fields comparing numbers and returns early on a duplicate, then push_back.
Why it might be faster: avoids the extra call and returned pointer of GetField on a hot path of message construction (about 1.4% at search time).

28.subject: MesgDefinition::GetFieldByIndex: raw data pointer and branch hint
28.body:
What: uses fields.data() and a __builtin_expect hint for the in-range case.
Why it might be faster: removes the vector operator[] indirection; effect is tiny (0.16% at search time) and within noise. __builtin_expect is a GCC/Clang extension.

31.subject: FieldBase::GetValue<T>: read fixed-size values with memcpy
31.body:
What: switches on the element size (1, 2, 4, 8 bytes) and loads the value with one memcpy instead of assembling it byte by byte in a loop; keeps the old loop as the fallback.
Why it might be faster: one load instead of up to eight shift/or steps per value (about 0.7% at search time).
Risk: assumes a little-endian host (the original loop was endian-independent); true for the x86-64 nodes used here. Adds #include <cstring>.

34.subject: Profile::GetMesg: table of pointers instead of indices
34.body:
What: the lookup table stores const MESG* directly (zero-initialised static), dropping the 0xFFFF fill loop and the index dereference.
Why it might be faster: one fewer step per lookup and a cheaper first call. Step measured 0.12%, within noise. Same thread-safety caveat as the earlier GetMesg change.

37.subject: Field::GetNumSubFields: branch hints on the null/range checks
37.body:
What: caches profile in a local and adds __builtin_expect hints.
Why it might be faster: probably marginal; measured 0.06% at search time, i.e. noise. Included only because the search accepted it.
